name: Butterbur
short: The plant contains liver-toxic pyrrolizidine alkaloids. Spontaneous reports link a defined extract to liver injury, including two liver transplants; such cases are rare.
text: Butterbur contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids, which are potentially toxic to the liver and carcinogenic, and a review of migraine treatments stated that butterbur needs to be free of these alkaloids to ensure safety. Liver injury has also been reported with a defined butterbur extract: in an analysis of spontaneous reports most affected people had mild liver test changes, but nine developed severe liver injury and two required liver transplantation; the authors judged such cases rare, idiosyncratic and frequently confounded by other medicines, noting that 22 patients had also taken medicines that can harm the liver. An earlier review noted four cases of reversible cholestatic hepatitis probably associated with long-term use and described other side effects as gastrointestinal and usually mild.
